I added open and close transitions to the account dropdown, the "Changes saved" toast and the delete-account modal. All three changes are in `src/styles.css`. `app.js` and `index.html` are unchanged, because the existing `hidden` and `.is-open` toggles now drive the transitions. I haven't checked any of it in a browser.

**How it works:** CSS can't normally animate an element that switches to or from `display: none`. Each overlay now starts from a hidden state set with `@starting-style`, and `transition-behavior: allow-discrete` keeps it on screen until its close transition finishes. The timings use your existing tokens: opening takes `--duration-medium` (250ms), closing takes the shorter `--duration-short` (150ms), and both use `--ease-standard`.

- **Account dropdown:** fades in and grows from 0.96 to full size, starting from its top-right corner because it's right-aligned under the button. It closes the same way, faster.
- **"Changes saved" toast:** fades in and rises 16px from the bottom edge, then drops back down as it fades out. I kept its existing `translate: -50%` centering in both states.
- **Delete-account modal:** the backdrop fades in and out, and the card grows from its center, from 0.96 to full size. The broken `transition: all 400ms ease` is gone. It never ran because the modal was jumping straight from `display: none`.
- **Reduced motion:** if someone has reduced motion turned on in their system settings, all three only fade, with no growing or sliding.

**Not tested:** I didn't open the page in a browser to watch the transitions or try reopening an overlay while it's still closing. Older browsers that lack `@starting-style` or discrete `display` transitions (both added in 2024) will just show and hide instantly, the way they do now.

One unrelated issue I left alone: the `.menu a:hover` style isn't limited to devices with a mouse, so on touch screens a tapped menu item can stay highlighted.

All three now have open and close transitions. The changes are CSS-only, in `src/styles.css`, so `app.js` and the markup are unchanged. I checked the code by reading it but didn't run it in a browser, so none of the motion has been watched yet.

**Why they popped:** toggling `hidden` or `display: none` gives the browser no previous style to animate from. The modal also had `transition: all 400ms ease`, and that can't animate out of `display: none`, so it showed and hid instantly. Each one now uses `@starting-style` for the first frame of the open state and `transition-behavior: allow-discrete`, which keeps the element visible until the close transition ends.

| Element | Opening | Closing |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Account dropdown | Fades in and grows from 0.96 scale out of its top-right corner, where the button is | Fades out and shrinks back toward the button |
| "Changes saved" toast | Fades in and slides up from the bottom edge of the screen | Fades out and slides back down off the bottom |
| Delete-account modal | Backdrop fades in; the card grows from 0.96 scale at its center | Same in reverse |

- **Timing:** everything uses the project's existing tokens. Opening takes `--duration-medium` (250ms) and closing the shorter `--duration-short` (150ms), both with `--ease-standard`.
- **Reversing mid-animation:** these are transitions, not keyframes, so clicking the dropdown button again while it's still opening reverses it smoothly instead of snapping.
- **Reduced motion:** the scaling and sliding only run when the user hasn't turned on "reduce motion". With it on, all three still fade in and out.
- **Older browsers:** this approach needs a 2024-or-later browser (Chrome 117+, Safari 17.5+, Firefox 129+). Older ones fall back to the current instant show and hide, so nothing breaks.

Three related issues I left alone:
- The modal doesn't close on Escape and doesn't move keyboard focus into or out of the dialog.
- The menu's hover background isn't limited to devices that can hover, so on touchscreens it can stay highlighted after a tap.
- The modal backdrop does nothing when clicked.

I added open and close transitions for all three in `src/styles.css`. I didn't need to change `app.js`, because it already shows and hides the dropdown and toast with `hidden` and the modal with `is-open`, and the CSS now animates those changes. I haven't run this in a browser, so I haven't watched the animations play.

**Why they popped:** all three switch between `display: none` and visible, and a normal CSS transition doesn't run across that switch. The modal also had `transition: all 400ms ease`, which did nothing. The fix uses `@starting-style` to give each element a starting state when it appears. `transition-behavior: allow-discrete` keeps it on screen until the close animation finishes.

**What each one does now:**
- **Account dropdown:** fades and grows from 0.96 to full size, starting from its top-right corner because it opens below the button, aligned to its right edge.
- **"Changes saved" toast:** fades in while rising 16px from the bottom of the screen, and sinks back down as it fades out. It stays horizontally centred throughout.
- **Delete-account modal:** the dimmed backdrop fades, and the card grows from 0.96 to full size from its centre.

**Timing:** openings take 250ms and closings 150ms, using the `--duration-medium`, `--duration-short` and `--ease-standard` values from `tokens.css`, so they match the rest of the project.

**Reduced motion:** if the user's system is set to reduce motion, the scaling and sliding are turned off and all three just fade in and out.

**Browser support:** this works in current Chrome, Safari and Firefox. Older browsers will show and hide the elements instantly, as they do now.

**Related issues I left alone:**
- The modal doesn't move keyboard focus into itself or close on Escape.
- The dropdown's hover style isn't limited to devices with a mouse, so it can stay highlighted after a tap on touchscreens.

I can fix either if you'd like.

The empty state now has a staggered entrance. I only changed `src/styles.css`; `index.html` didn't need any edits. I haven't checked it in a browser.

**How it enters:** the folder icon, the "No projects yet" title, the description and the two buttons come in one after another, 100ms apart. Each one fades in, moves up 12px and goes from slightly blurred to sharp over 300ms. The whole thing finishes in about 0.6 seconds.

**Reduced motion:** if someone has asked their system for reduced motion, the pieces just fade in, in the same order, without moving or blurring.

**If animation doesn't run:** the content is still shown, because it's only hidden at the very start of the animation.

**When it plays:** every time the page loads with no projects, not only on someone's very first visit. If you want it to play only once per person, I can add a small script that remembers it has already played (for example in `localStorage`) and skips the animation after that.

The empty state now has a staged entrance. I only changed `src/styles.css`; `index.html` is untouched.

- **The sequence:** the folder icon, the "No projects yet" heading, the description and the two buttons come in one after another, 100ms apart. Each one fades in, rises 12px and goes from a slight blur to sharp over 300ms. The whole thing takes about 0.6s.
- **Reduced motion:** if someone has "reduce motion" turned on, each piece just fades in on the same timing, with no movement or blur.
- **If the animation doesn't run:** the hidden state exists only at the start of the animation, so if it never plays for any reason, the content still shows normally rather than staying invisible.

It plays once each time the page loads. Since this page is static HTML, the empty state is only ever drawn on load, so it won't replay later. If you later render it with JavaScript, it will replay whenever it's added back to the page.

I haven't checked it in a browser. The timing and the reduced-motion fade come from reading the CSS, not from watching it run.

The empty state now enters in stages: the icon, the "No projects yet" heading, the description and the action buttons appear one after another, 100ms apart. I only changed `src/styles.css`; `index.html` is untouched. I haven't looked at it in a browser, so the timing and feel haven't been checked on screen.

- **Motion:** each part fades in, rises 12px and goes from slightly blurred to sharp over 300ms. The whole sequence takes about 0.6s.
- **Reduced motion:** for people who have reduced motion turned on in their system settings, each part only fades in, with no movement or blur.
- **Fallback:** the content is only hidden at the very start of the animation, so it stays visible if animations don't run.

Decision for you: this page is static HTML with no app logic, so the entrance plays on every load of the empty state, not only the very first visit. Limiting it to the first visit would need a small script that remembers a visit (for example in `localStorage`) and skips the animation after that. I'd leave it as it is, because the animation is short and an empty state usually only appears until someone creates a project. I can add the script if you want it to play once.
